actions: Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller, and any other refrigeration controller with a remote management interface because not every second-wave site's vendor is confirmed, in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap, and CERT-FR asks you to check your insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.

On every such controller that was reachable from the internet, check the whole configuration, defrost ranges, alarm thresholds and notification recipients included, against the intended one, verify the actual temperatures and test that alarms reach staff; for a Danfoss unit that may have been taken over, restart it or otherwise factory-reset it, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network and reconfigure it for service, then update its firmware, set the security level to Strict and replace the default and any weak passwords, which do not close the six unpatched AK-SM 800A flaws that Midnight Blue and CCB report, so the interface stays off the internet; change all credentials where compromise is suspected and check the devices attached to the controllers, as BSI advises; and on every Copeland or Dixell XWEB unit confirm the factory Admin password was changed and give each contractor a named account with an expiry date.

items.headline: Danfoss AK-SM 800A: six unpatched pre-auth RCE flaws, Strict mode does not remove them; France blames IRGC
items.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of French stores, and on 2026-11-09 France's foreign ministry attributed that campaign, and only that campaign, to the Iranian unit Shahid Kaveh. More followed: more than 115 stores in at least six more countries and the first German shops on 2026-11-02, altered cold-room settings at three sites of the French blood service through a supplier, and, per SRF on 2026-11-05, a Köniz butcher and three Volg stores in Switzerland. CERT-FR reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, and NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited. On 2026-11-11 Midnight Blue reported six pre-authentication remote-code-execution flaws in all Danfoss AK-SM 800A firmware up to 5.3.2, and on 2026-11-20 Danfoss published CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.3, an unauthenticated stack overflow in AK-SM 8xxA firmware 5.4.0 and earlier, fix only in an announced 5.5.x) and CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS 9.9, default credentials on every legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800, no fix); CCB says updating, new passwords and Strict mode are insufficient, so removing internet exposure comes first, and BACS's statement of 2026-11-10 that updates fix the known flaws predates the report and does not cover the six.

items.headline: Java4Shell: OpenJDK Base64 heap overflow chained to pre-auth RCE in Jira and Keycloak; update Java, attempts seen
items.summary: Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update and the OpenJDK advisory of 2026-11-17 fix CVE-2026-114938, an out-of-bounds write in the AVX-512 Base64 decoder that Calif, its discoverer, scores CVSS 4.0 9.2 and says it turned into pre-authentication code execution in the default configurations of Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate; Oracle scores it CVSS 3.1 8.1 with high attack complexity. Only x86-64 hosts with AVX-512 VBMI are affected, a trigger proof of concept is public, Calif withholds its product chains, a second researcher claims a working exploit with no release stated, GreyNoise reports exploitation attempts without a confirmed success against its sensors, and VulnCheck says a working exploit is available to its customers. NCSC.ch and BACS warn operators to update internet-reachable Java applications and identity services first, and Cisco's advisory, at version 1.3, lists Catalyst Center, IOS XE and ISE as not affected while Siemens lists Siveillance Control, Siveillance Control Pro and Industrial Edge Management Pro and Virtual with no fix yet.

items.headline: NGINX nginx2root: five unauthenticated flaws reach worker RCE, Rapid7 PoC public; update 1.31.9, 1.30.7 or Plus 37.3.0.1
items.summary: F5 and the nginx project fixed five memory-corruption flaws in the nginx data plane on 2026-11-18, two in HTTP/2 and one each in HTTP/3, the resolver and the mail proxy, which CERT-EU says can lead to unauthenticated code execution with the privileges of the worker process; NCSC-NL scores all five CVSS 4.0 9.2, NCSC.ch and Wiz the two HTTP/2 flaws and Rapid7 CVE-2026-123007. The fixes are in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, while NGINX Plus R33 to R36 have no update. Rapid7 published a proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007, CERT-EU reports no exploitation, and NCSC.ch, CERT-EU, CERT.at and NCSC-NL issued warnings. Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled as affected, Cisco and Siemens list products with fixes pending or none, and Fortinet is still investigating its portfolio.

items.headline: Cisco Expressway root RCE is exploited (CISA KEV, F6 incident): upgrade clustered units to X15.5.20 and check them
items.summary: Cisco's disclosure of 2026-10-21 fixes CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 3.1 9.8), which lets an unauthenticated attacker who holds persistent cookies run operating-system commands as root on Expressway-C and Expressway-E configured in a cluster; X15.5.3 and earlier get X15.5.20, X14 and earlier must migrate, and there is no workaround. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20, and F6 reports that, soon after a public proof of concept appeared, attackers compromised two internet-reachable X15.5.3 devices, reached two internal cluster nodes through one and ran Python scripts for scanning and credential theft, while Cisco's advisory still says it knows of no malicious use. The same-day hardening releases for the Unified CM family and Unity Connection (up to 9.8, fixed in 15SU5) and for Snort 3 (9.0) are not known to be exploited.

Zammad 7.2.2 (2026-10-08) fixes the root escalation, which affects only DEB and RPM (packager.io) installations, Zammad 7.2.3 of 2026-11-11, a critical security update, supersedes it, and 6.5.5 (2026-10-15) is an emergency fix for the code-execution flaw in the otherwise unsupported 6.5 series; 7.2.1 (2026-10-06) had fixed 27 newly published advisories in 7.2.0 and earlier, two rated critical, none with a CVE id and none reported exploited.

items.headline: Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13, 3.3.14 fix seven memory flaws; a Rails exploit is announced for 25 November: update the interpreter
items.summary: The Ruby project released 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 on 2026-11-18 for seven memory-corruption flaws in the regexp engine and in string case conversion, three rated Critical, and says it knows of proofs of concept that reach remote code execution. Veria Labs, which found the case-conversion flaw independently (CVE-2026-132825, a one-byte heap overflow), says Rails and classic-style Sinatra are exposed without authentication in their default configuration and plans to publish a code-execution proof of concept on stock Rails on 25 November 2026; no exploitation is reported. Ruby 3.2 and earlier are end of life, and the interpreter itself, not a gem, must be updated.

items.headline: OptimJack: Optimizely names the exploited signup-flow flaw; Report URI counts 178 organisations, Zscaler 450+ domains
items.summary: Optimizely says an unauthorized party exploited a flaw in its Web Experimentation account signup flow to impersonate users and add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects, fewer than 5% of its customers, and Report URI counts 178 organisations that served the code on 2026-11-16 while Zscaler ThreatLabz counts more than 450 domains; the Optimizely files carry a crypto clipper and card skimmer. Ohey reports that scripts served by Kissmetrics and StorifyMe gained a loader from 2026-11-13 that routes iPhones to the Coruna and DarkSword exploit-kit stages and that minute-ly's loader was replaced outright; Hudson Rock names 21 web properties, among them the University of Basel's StorifyMe widget, and calls the iPhone stages delivery observations, not confirmed compromises. How the Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly files were altered is unknown.

items.headline: N-central: Hotfix 3 fixes 17 more CVEs and blocks the Legacy API; 4EverAble2Shell exploited; upgrade Agents too
items.summary: An independent researcher published proof-of-concept code on 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09 for what Huntress counts as 33 critical flaws in N-able's N-central appliance, and a second disclosure on 2026-11-12 added 4EverAble2Shell, a chain through Apache Axis (CVE-2026-90436) that works against Hotfix 2 when the Legacy API is on and is exploited on at least 21 production servers, and Agent2Shell, SYSTEM commands on managed Windows endpoints. Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26, 2026-11-10) fixed seven CVE ids and Hotfix 3 (build 2026.4.1.39, 2026-11-16) fixes 17 more, hardens how Agents and Probes authenticate and blocks the Legacy API permanently, but N-able does not name either chain or say it is fixed; Huntress reports public proof-of-concept code for all 17 and no exploitation of them in its partners' environments. Every on-premises server and every Agent and Probe must be on Hotfix 3, including those already on Hotfix 2.

items.headline: TYPO3: backend user to installer to admin and RCE (SA-027 Critical); Form Framework flaw SA-029 exploited; update now
items.summary: TYPO3 published ten core advisories on 2026-11-17 for 10.0.0 to 14.3.11, fixed in 14.3.12 LTS, 13.4.40 LTS, 12.4.52 ELTS, 11.5.57 ELTS and 10.4.63 ELTS. TYPO3 states that SA-029, a Medium information disclosure in the Form Framework that can become cross-site scripting through uploaded HTML, is known to be actively exploited, naming no actor or victim.

actions: Update every ScreenConnect technician host client and Access agent to 26.6.5 or later now, not only the server, because the vulnerable code runs on the technician's machine; where that waits, remove the TransferFiles permission from every role and session group (Administration > Security > Roles).

Treat any pre-26.6.5 client that shows a second, unfamiliar RMM tool or an unexplained ScreenConnect connection ID as compromised and reimage it rather than patching in place, because a technician's session can already have propagated the infection to every host that client connected to.

items.summary: CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9) lets file-transfer actions inside an already-active ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote session run without the authorization or Host-confirmation step the product is meant to require. items.headline: Fortinet advisories: FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager 8.0 have no fix for a 9.8 JSON API flaw; FortiMail RCE rows too
items.summary: Fortinet's hardening releases of 2026-10-21 (FortiMail, FortiAuthenticator) and 2026-10-22 (FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer) fixed critical and high-severity flaws, and the advisories withheld until Patch Tuesday were published on 2026-11-10 with critical rows in FortiMail (unauthenticated code execution, SQL injection and IBE account takeover, CVSS up to 9.8), FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager (an unauthenticated JSON API flaw at 9.8, oftp port flaws, FGFM code execution), FortiOS, FortiAuthenticator and FortiClient. items.summary: Huntress observed from 2026-10-07 23:20 UTC attackers chaining two AhsayCBS flaws, CVE-2026-105133 (authentication bypass) and CVE-2026-105134 (code execution as SYSTEM through the Replication Receiver API), against internet-exposed servers of the backup management console that managed service providers and system integrators mainly use, dropping JSP webshells and an XMRig cryptominer; Bitdefender MDR investigated three intrusions through the same chain, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14. items.headline: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
items.summary: PK Softech AG, the software supplier of Publica and other Swiss pension funds, says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT and that data must be assumed to have left; the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating and has added the case to its criminal proceeding against Akira. Tamedia reports that Akira holds about 100 GB and demands ransom, while PK Softech and the federal bodies say no concrete ransom demand reached them; Publica and several other funds say their insured persons' personal data has presumably left. Cantonal police warn that criminals could use leaked personal and financial data for investment-fraud calls.

items.summary: VulnCheck, as CNA, published 14 CVEs on 2026-11-12 for XWEB EVO, the end-of-service Copeland and Dixell web supervisor for refrigeration and cold-chain equipment, seven of them scored CVSS 4.0 9.2 to 9.3: unauthenticated command injection that runs as root, a hard-coded Administrator password, and Administrator and root passwords computed from the device MAC address and date. The injection flaws are fixed on the current firmware branch, while the password flaws reach the last firmware, 5.8.8, and stay unfixed because Copeland ended software support on 2026-03-16; Copeland tells operators to remove all XWEB EVO units from the public internet.

items.headline: Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla: anonymous Super User flaws exploited since July; update to 2.20.5.0
items.summary: The mySites.guru research campaign against Joomla third-party extensions produced six further disclosures between 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-23, and one of them changes technique class: the Balbooa Gridbox page builder (CVE-2026-61425) trusts a client-supplied cookie value as proof of identity, so setting an administrator's username in that cookie authenticates the requester as that user with no password and no existing session. A Joomla Super User can edit templates, which is PHP execution, so this is full site compromise from a single anonymous request. Fixed in Gridbox 2.20.1; the researcher says the vulnerable code shipped for at least nine months. The same week added unauthenticated SQL injection and order-forgery flaws in EasyStore, an invoice IDOR in Events Booking, and a critical unauthenticated upload in Membership Pro. A follow-up audit of Gridbox produced eleven more CVEs, fixed in 2.20.2, four of them exploited in the wild, and Gridbox 2.20.3.1 (21 September) fixes a further unauthenticated SQL injection present in every earlier build. Gridbox 2.20.4.2 (27 October) fixes two more unauthenticated SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, with no exploitation reported, and Gridbox version 2.20.5.0 (4 November) fixes four more flaws, the worst an unauthenticated file deletion, also with no exploitation reported.

items.headline: Entra app-credential abuse: agents hunt GitHub for secrets, an operator reaches MSP clients, government among them
items.summary: Microsoft reports that since August threat actors have used the agentic framework ARTEX to query public GitHub for OAuth application secrets and cloud keys, and that from 2026-10-28 valid application credentials were used for service-principal sign-ins across dozens of applications in several tenants, a vendor-owned multitenant application among them. Todyl's telemetry shows one operator since 2026-11-01 targeting about 45 application registrations at MSPs, more than 33 of which authenticated, and reaching 27 organisations, government clients among them; Microsoft says a similar campaign involving the same addresses was reported by Todyl, and Todyl's update of 2026-11-06 now assesses its operator as an automated agentic credential crawler, likely fed by secrets exposed in public repositories or web apps.

items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, though its own copy of the attacker's chain got no shell. items.headline: Apache Roller XML-RPC deserialization RCE is exploited and on CISA KEV; upgrade to 6.1.6 or later

items.headline: FBI: various actors run ARTEX against many sectors, government included; Microsoft names Storm-0940 and Storm-3358
items.summary: Microsoft reports that since at least September 2026 Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, has used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth-application abuse against hundreds of organizations across many industries including government, reaching privileged cloud access in under three hours in several cases; Expel saw the same infrastructure create its own accounts through Okta self-service registration. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report on 2026-10-31 that since late August they have seen ARTEX, PentAGI and CAIRN operated in incident-response cases, with ARTEX adopted by extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters whose victims include US government organizations, and that the original ARTEX repository was taken down in October while forks keep it in circulation. CrowdStrike and Recorded Future document another actor using the framework, and Seoul police referred a criminal group's leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for extorting 38 of more than 90 organizations, with the same framework according to BleepingComputer. Microsoft adds on 2026-11-06 another cluster, the Cambodia-based, financially motivated Storm-3358 targeting financial organisations, and Check Point reads ten exposed operator consoles that show near-autonomous, opportunistic ARTEX campaigns. CERT-EU says AI-driven activity against the EU institutions it protects highly likely involved ARTEX. The FBI's FLASH of 2026-11-13 says a variety of actors have used ARTEX since at least August against sectors including financial services, government, technology and defense, and lists the observed techniques, among them cloud-trust and vendor-credential pivots, Kudu abuse and Active Directory credential theft.

items.headline: ESET: Turla's Cereal runs the victim's own Exchange server as C2 and wraps transport agents to collect mail
items.summary: ESET found a previously undocumented .NET toolset, Cereal, on a Kazakh government organisation's Exchange server in November 2025 and on a Romanian government organisation's from December 2025, and attributes it to Turla with high confidence. The compromised Exchange server is the command channel, answering requests on web paths that imitate Outlook Web Access, Autodiscover and ActiveSync, and a module injected into the transport service wraps existing transport agents to collect mail, in Romania configured to select messages to or from NATO and EU addresses; ESET could not determine the initial access method.

items.headline: PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36: FPM request smuggling to code execution; the open session flaw is fixed
items.summary: The PHP project released 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and 8.6.0 on 2026-11-19 with fixes for up to 18 CVEs per branch. The most direct is CVE-2026-129289: PHP-FPM keeps unread php://input bytes on a persistent FastCGI connection, so an unauthenticated multipart request can plant a second FastCGI request and run PHP code as the worker, but only behind a front end that reuses FastCGI connections, which standard nginx and Apache setups do not. The release also fixes CVE-2026-115560, left open in October, and follow-ups to an incomplete earlier fix; no source reports exploitation or a public proof of concept.

items.headline: Cyderes: 'tcherber' VPN toolkit for FortiGate and SonicWall, credential file mixing default and real logins, LDAP sweep
items.summary: Cyderes' Howler Cell recovered a Go toolkit that wraps OpenConnect for FortiGate and NetExtender for SonicWall, a credential file of more than 500 FortiGate entries mixing default guest, admin and test logins with organisation-specific passwords, and VPN connection logs showing sustained root-level tunnels into multiple victim environments in May and June 2026. Once the tunnel is up the orchestrator maps internal routes and enumerates Active Directory over LDAP, while port scanning, SMB reconnaissance and credential validation are manual tools. Cyderes assesses a Russian-speaking initial access broker and malware-as-a-service seller and names no victim, vulnerability or firmware version.

items.headline: Symantec: attacker ran SYSTEM commands on a domain controller through CyberPower PowerPanel Business, then took ntds.dit
items.summary: Symantec analysed an intrusion in which the attacker used CyberPower PowerPanel Business, UPS-management software, as an execution channel on a Windows domain controller: scripts placed in the product's extcmd folder run through the ppbed.exe service as SYSTEM, and the operator iterated scripts until ntds.dit was exported with ntdsutil ifm and esentutl /vss, then side-loaded an implant. Symantec does not say how the attacker reached the console (public advisories or stolen administrator credentials could give that access) and names no actor.

items.headline: Idunno.AntiCsrf (ASP.NET WebForms) unauthenticated deserialization RCE exploited, no patch: remove the module
items.summary: Mandiant published CVE-2026-131914 on 2026-11-18 for Idunno.AntiCsrf, an open-source anti-CSRF HTTP module for ASP.NET WebForms last released in December 2008: any anonymously reachable page that does not opt out passes a crafted CSRF form field to an unvalidated deserializer, so one POST runs code in the IIS worker process (CVSS 4.0 9.3). items.headline: Barracuda: an unretired vendor cloud key led an ARTEX-consistent intruder across ten accounts in 44 hours
items.summary: Barracuda says an attacker used a valid cloud access key that it had issued to an AI-sector vendor for a past project and never retired, between 2026-11-01 04:33 and 2026-11-02 23:31 UTC, reading stored secrets and moving through about ten cloud accounts, a data analytics system, a source-code token and Kubernetes clusters. items.headline: Mandiant: COLD RELIC turns one cloud compromise into the pretext for the next; enrolled passkeys outlive password resets
items.summary: Mandiant reports that COLD RELIC, the name Google Threat Intelligence Group now uses for the group formerly tracked as COLDRIVER and UNC4057 (Star Blizzard), reused the staff directory and identities stolen from one US organisation in late 2025 to impersonate a contact when approaching a second in 2026. items.headline: eMudhra: eight ECDSA CA keys guessable, eight RSA CAs revoked; Windows drops the rest 2026-11-16; update clients
items.summary: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were so weak that anyone could recover them and forge trusted HTTPS certificates for any site, and eMudhra's incident report of 2026-11-10 adds eight RSA intermediates revoked on 2026-11-07 because it cannot show their keys were handled as its policy requires. Browsers and the Apple, Microsoft and Google trust stores block the eight ECDSA intermediates, and Microsoft removes the remaining eMudhra roots from Windows, Edge and WebView2 from 2026-11-16. Software with its own trust store or no revocation checking stays exposed until updated (Go, GitLab, Python, Java, macOS command-line tools, SonicWall DPI-SSL, Cisco IOS XE and ISE), and no exploitation is reported.

items.headline: Brotli flaw: Apple fixes iOS, macOS; Siemens WinCC, UMC, Teamcenter, Opcenter mostly unfixed; Mitel, Cisco listed
items.summary: Between 2026-10-27 and 2026-11-13 Siemens, Mitel and Cisco listed affected products in advisories that cover the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497: Siemens names Desigo CC V8 and V9 (remedy: the latest .NET security updates), Gridscale X DSA V5.3 and Gridscale X PSS®E below V36.8.0 (fixed in V5.4 and V36.8.0), Industrial Edge, where Common Configurator has no fix, and, in two interim advisories of 2026-11-10, 15 industrial products including SIMATIC WinCC V7/V8, WinCC Unified, the User Management Component and TIA Administrator and 28 software products including Teamcenter and the Opcenter family, nearly all with no fix; Mitel names MiVoice Business and five OpenScape products with updates planned and workaround articles for three; Cisco's combined advisory lists Duo Network Gateway (3.4.2), RoomOS and, at version 1.13 of 2026-11-13, Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches running Guest Shell among its products with fixes, a longer list of which is dated up to 2027, without saying which of its CVEs each fix addresses. Cisco says it is not aware of malicious use against any Cisco product, and CISA lists the flaw as exploited. Apple fixed the flaw on 2026-11-09 in iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 and 26.7.3, macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, Tahoe 26.7.3 and Sequoia 15.8.3, watchOS 27.2.1 and visionOS 27.2.1, and in HomeView Software 27.2 on 2026-11-12 and tvOS 27.2.1 on 2026-11-13.

items.headline: Insikt: GhostFrame implant re-disables ESXi execInstalledOnly every five seconds and steals guest credentials
items.summary: Recorded Future's Insikt Group describes GhostFrame, a command-and-control and post-exploitation framework for VMware ESXi hosts that operators must already hold root on: its vmhostd-core implant persists through ESXi boot scripts, disables the ESXi firewall and the execInstalledOnly control about every five seconds, and a web panel controls guest VMs and runs VMkatz against memory snapshots and virtual disks to recover Windows credentials. Insikt links it to TAG-218, whose activity overlaps Settra ransomware and whose servers targeted SonicWall, Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet VPN appliances in the US and Europe from late August to October 2026.

actions: On every internet-facing Linux server and every XenServer or XCP-ng host with its Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager appliances, install the vendor's fixed kernel or firmware and reboot, then confirm the running version.

items.headline: Linux TCP use-after-free: Sophos hotfix and Ubuntu generic kernels out; WatchGuard, Fortinet have no fixed build
items.summary: The Linux kernel CVE team published CVE-2026-98432 on 2026-10-15, a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP connection setup path that dates to Linux 4.4 and is reached by a SYN packet carrying IP options; the CNA scores it CVSS 9.8. Anthropic reports that Claude wrote an exploit giving a remote, unauthenticated attacker root on servers with a multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener, which CloudLinux's kernel team could not reproduce; the Go team says the bug is not specific to MPTCP and Akamai that disabling MPTCP does not prevent exploitation, and no source reports attacks. Citrix rates its XenServer 8.4 and 9 bulletin Critical and names fixes for Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager, XCP-ng released a kernel fix, MikroTik's RouterOS 7.25.1 and 7.24.6 list the CVE, Red Hat, Debian, CIQ and Amazon Linux kernels are fixed, Ubuntu has fixed its generic kernels for 22.04 to 26.10 while 20.04 and older and some HWE, FIPS, NVIDIA and Azure variant kernels were still in progress on 2026-11-10, and Sophos has shipped a Firewall hotfix and SD-RED firmware, while WatchGuard (Fireware OS, AP, Dimension) and Fortinet list their products as unresolved or under investigation without a fixed build, Fortinet offering an IPS virtual patch.

actions: On every musl-based Linux host that runs sshd (Alpine, OpenWrt, Buildroot, Yocto), install OpenSSH 10.6p2 or the distribution's fixed openssh package and restart sshd, because updating the package does not replace the running server, and rebuild container and cloud images from a fixed base; until then set PasswordAuthentication no in sshd_config and restart sshd.

On each such host that allowed password logins while reachable, search the sshd log for an accepted password on an account whose password field is *, and check root's and the default alpine user's authorized_keys for keys nobody added and the init scripts for a service nobody installed, because CISA lists the flaw as exploited and GreyNoise saw both persistence steps.

items.headline: CISA lists the OpenSSH musl password bypass as exploited; update to 10.6p2 or turn passwords off
items.summary: OpenSSH Portable 10.6p2 of 2026-11-05 works around CVE-2026-123158, a password-authentication bypass on Linux systems that use musl libc and run sshd without PAM, Alpine's default OpenSSH server and OpenWrt among them: a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes logs in to an account whose password field is *. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory the same day and has rated the flaw actively exploited since 2026-11-10; Alpine shipped fixed packages for every branch back to 3.16. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-09, and GreyNoise records hands-on logins on its gridpoints from 2026-11-07 that ended in a dropped Python implant; SANS ISC's sensors record attempts from 2026-11-05 and Previdian's from 2026-11-06, QNAP says its NAS systems are not affected, and no source reports a compromised production host.

items.headline: Huntress: 2,223 crypto-named fake sessions sit on 118 ScreenConnect servers, likely bait for unpatched technicians
items.summary: Huntress counted 2,223 unauthorized guest sessions on 118 self-hosted ScreenConnect servers at 109 MSP and organisation accounts, enrolled between 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-13 and named after crypto exchanges; on the 29 servers with complete history an operator revisited every 151 seconds to keep them online. Huntress's leading hypothesis, which it has not observed, is that they are bait for a technician with a client older than 26.6.5 to connect, so that CVE-2026-84869 runs a file on the technician's workstation; it saw no malicious activity from the sessions and found no overlap with the SCKit indicators.

actions: Search every branch of your organisation's and suppliers' GitHub repositories for a semicolon followed by 200 or more spaces in JavaScript, TypeScript and build configuration files, and for .vscode/tasks.json tasks that run node when a folder opens; on any hit, rotate every GitHub and npm token reachable from the developer machines and CI runners that built the repository and review force-pushes, deploy keys, Actions secrets and releases since the infection, because deleting the loader does not revoke the access that pushed it.
items.headline: PolinRider: forged backdated commits, npm hijacks and a fake recruiter run a loader at build or folder open
items.summary: Apiiro found the PolinRider loader in at least 7,609 GitHub repositories owned by 2,330 accounts, where stolen GitHub access force-pushes a copy of the owner's own commit, with the same author, message and date, plus a loader hidden after hundreds of spaces in a build configuration file. Sonatype found the same loader in 12 hijacked npm releases and JFrog in a fake employer's take-home test and scripted camera check; none relies on an npm install script, the server address is read from an Ethereum wallet, and removing the code does not revoke the access that pushed it.

actions: On every developer endpoint that runs Cursor, check extension-install telemetry for Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 installed between 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29; where it is found, isolate the host, remove the unauthorized SSH key, the persistence and any running tunnel process, because uninstalling the extension removes none of them, and rotate every credential reachable from the host from a trusted system.

Ask the admin of every Cursor team your organisation uses whether Cursor's email listing exposed keys arrived, and rotate every key it lists, because Cursor says coding-agent traces from sessions outside Privacy Mode held unredacted credentials.
items.headline: Cursor marketplace served a trojanised Claude Code extension for 11 hours; uninstalling leaves the SSH backdoor
items.summary: Between about 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29 the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace served a modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows, that appends an attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys, tries to enable SSH and open a reverse tunnel, and installs persistence that outlives the extension; coding errors made the SSH step fail on most standard-user hosts, so Cursor says the attacker could not log in there. Cursor's report of 2026-11-13 says the chain began with an access key it had issued to its vendor Fireworks AI, exposed by Fireworks, which gave the attacker a storage bucket of coding-agent traces holding some unredacted credentials, and that a stolen credential from the exposed data let the attacker write the extension straight onto the marketplace cache; Cursor says this was not a vulnerability in Anthropic's product.

items.headline: Red Hat Quay: anonymous signing-key takeover and cross-tenant token theft; update to your branch's fixed release
items.summary: Red Hat's CNA records say an unauthenticated client of Red Hat Quay can obtain an anonymous registry token, present it to the service-key rotation endpoint and install its own signing key (CVE-2026-123710, CVSS 3.1 9.8), and that an account that can create a namespace containing an underscore can retrieve other tenants' robot tokens (CVE-2026-110697, 9.9). items.headline: Group-IB: DarkLunnen's FortiOS chain leaves a 'service' super_admin; Swiss FortiGates are scan targets only
items.summary: Group-IB found an open directory on a Latvian server that documents more than 14 months of operations against Europe by an operator it tracks as DarkLunnen and links to no known actor: a modified public exploit for FortiOS CVE-2024-55591 that creates an administrator named service with super_admin privileges, among other tools. Group-IB recovered a list of 4,725 Swiss FortiGate scanning targets, which it says does not confirm vulnerability or exploitation, and restic commands that accessed an S3 backup repository at a Swiss domain in May and June 2025, without naming an organisation or confirming success.

actions: In every GitHub organisation you or your suppliers administer, search for pull requests titled "docs: dependency audit notes" and for commits titled "ci: refresh build cache", "ci: restore", "ci: cleanup", "chore: add ci helper" or "chore: add dependency audit workflow"; for each account that pushed one, revoke its tokens, rotate every secret its workflows could read and remove the AWS trust-policy changes, access keys and Azure federated credentials the stealer created, because the persistence is designed to outlast rotation.
items.headline: WFX Phantom: stolen GitHub tokens push a CI stealer; cloud persistence meant to survive rotation; check for probe PRs
items.summary: StepSecurity and Aikido report that from 2026-11-10 an attacker uses stolen GitHub tokens, not a GitHub Actions bug, to open probe pull requests titled "docs: dependency audit notes" and then push a stealer script into workflows, CI scripts or npm hooks where the token's permissions allow, taking Actions secrets, runner memory and cloud credentials, planting AWS and Azure persistence and deleting the workflow runs. Counts differ by lab and time (more than 63,000 probes; at least 1,835 repositories where the payload ran); how the tokens were obtained is unknown, and no Swiss victim is named.

items.headline: LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI and in the official images stole cloud and AI credentials; removing the package does not stop it
items.summary: On 2026-10-21 LiteLLM 1.107.0, the open-source LLM gateway, shipped with malicious Python startup files in all seven PyPI wheels (live 11:39 to 13:23 UTC) and in the official GHCR and Docker Hub images behind the v1.107.0, latest, main-latest and main-stable tags (11:46 to 14:20 UTC); they run a credential stealer at every Python start and start a background loader that could execute code fetched from an attacker-chosen host, though Socket saw its pointer empty at 13:01 UTC. The maintainers' root-cause post of 2026-10-23 says an administrative key committed to a public repository on 2026-05-27 and never revoked gave the attacker, from 2026-10-10, a GitHub organization owner's CLI token, with which it stole two maintainers' tokens and, on 2026-10-21, overrode branch protection to build the release from a look-alike repository; Socket independently found secret-stealing workflows running on 2026-10-10. Wiz saw stolen AWS instance-role credentials tested about 4.5 hours after exfiltration; PyPI and the registries removed the release the same day and the maintainers say to pin 1.106.2 or an explicit earlier version.

items.headline: Android 'SMS of Death': one hidden SMS drops calls, emergency calls included; Android 12 and 13 get no fix
items.summary: An independent researcher published a working proof of concept on 2026-10-29 for a zero-click remote denial of service in Android's telephony framework: one malformed WAP Push data message crashes the com.android.phone process, drops active calls including emergency calls and, because the message is retried, can leave a phone in a restart loop. Google's November 2026 bulletin lists CVE-2026-58882, the identifier BleepingComputer gives for the flaw, as a critical denial of service fixed at the 2026-11-01 security patch level for Android 14 to 17 (the researcher had named the October update); Android 12 and 13 phones run the same code unfixed, and no source reports exploitation.

items.headline: PHP2Shell: Xerox fixes AltaLink 82xx/81xx, EC81xx and VersaLink; WorkCentre gets an interim patch, Fiery due 9-23 Nov
items.summary: Xerox's security bulletin XRX26-016, updated on 2026-11-06, marks AltaLink 82xx and 81xx, EC81xx and VersaLink C/B415, C/B625 and C/B620 as remediated by releases that add PHP 8.2.35 against the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. WorkCentre 3655, EC7836 and EC7856 and the newly listed AltaLink C8030 to C8070, AltaLink B8045 to B8090, EC8036 and EC8056 stay affected with a system software patch that Xerox says reduces exposure; Fiery patches are due between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-23 and the Worldwide Ticketing Tool fix is in development. The bulletin gives no statement on exploitation of Xerox devices, and CISA lists both PHP flaws as exploited.

items.headline: PHP2Shell hits QNAP NAS before login: QTS, QuTS hero, QVR, TVR OS, Notes Station 3 and QNE all have fixed builds
items.summary: QNAP's advisory QSA-26-18 says the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2) affect the PHP in the web components of QTS, QuTS hero, QuTScloud and several QNAP applications and can be triggered before authentication, and fixed builds dated 2026-10-23 are out for QTS, QuTS hero and QuTScloud. As of 2026-10-28 (revision V1.2) the table lists QVR Surveillance (ARM32) 3.0.3.1756, TVR OS 1.0.5 and Notes Station 3 3.9.15 as resolved; QNE (ADRA) has its own advisory, QSA-26-19, which since 2026-11-02 lists QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7.q327 as the fix; QNAP has seen scanning and exploitation attempts in the wild but no reports of exploitation targeting its products, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26. Synology's advisory, revised on 2026-10-31, fixes its PHP packages (except the end-of-life PHP 7.3), Mail Station and Calendar, with builds for DSM 7.2 and above, DSM 7.0 to 7.1 and, for PHP 7.4, Mail Station and Calendar, DSM 6.2.
